concepts.title: Splitting Numbers with Floor Division and Modulus
concepts.definition: Floor division (//) keeps only the whole part of a quotient, while modulus (%) keeps only the remainder; together they split a number into its digits, since the last digit is the remainder on division by 10 and the rest is the floor quotient.
concepts.key_idea: Dividing by 10 with // drops the final digit, and taking % 10 keeps it.
question_patterns: What do the expressions 13 // 4 and 13 % 4 evaluate to in Python?
Split the number 347 into its last digit and its remaining leading digits using // and %.
A number 86 ends in which digit, and what remains after that digit is removed?
Explain the difference between the / operator and the // operator with one example of each.
Find the sum of the last two digits of 275 using modulus and floor division.
The exponent operator is applied as 3 ** 4. What value does Python print?

solution_steps.explain: The remainder on division by 10 is the units digit.
Floor division by 10 removes the units digit.

solution_steps.action: add the tens and units digits
solution_steps.explain: The new last digit of the leading part is the tens digit.

worked_examples.q: Using the modulus operator, what is the last digit of 374?

concepts.title: Operator Precedence in Expressions
concepts.definition: Python evaluates an expression by applying operators in order of precedence: exponentiation first, then unary signs, then multiply-divide-modulus, then add-subtract, with equal-precedence operators working left to right and parentheses overriding everything.
concepts.key_idea: Parentheses beat every rule, so adding them is how you force a different evaluation order.

concepts.title: Logical Errors and Debugging
concepts.definition: A logical (semantic) error lets a program run to completion but prints wrong results, unlike a syntax error which stops execution and a runtime error which aborts a running program, for example division by zero.
concepts.key_idea: The only clue to a logical error is output that looks plausible but is wrong, so work backwards from the result.
question_patterns: The code 10 + 12/2 was meant to average 10 and 12. What does it print, and why is it wrong?
Classify these as syntax, logical or runtime errors: dividing by zero, a missing closing bracket, adding instead of averaging.
How does a logical error differ from a syntax error?
The average of two numbers 10 and 12 should be 11. Correct the faulty expression and give the right value.
Why can a program with a logical error be harder to catch than one with a syntax error?

solution_steps.explain: Without brackets, only the second number is halved first.
Brackets force the sum before halving.
The gap between the two results quantifies the bug.

worked_examples.q: Which error kind lets a program finish but print a wrong result: syntax, logical or runtime?

concepts.title: Simple Interest and Amount Payable
concepts.definition: Money lent at simple interest grows by principal times rate times years divided by 100, and the amount to repay is the principal plus that interest.
concepts.key_idea: Simple interest accrues on the original principal alone, never on accumulated interest.
question_patterns: Write a Python program that inputs principal, rate and time and prints the simple interest and the amount payable.
A loan of 5000 runs at 6 percent per annum for 2 years. Compute the simple interest.
For principal 8000 at 7.5 percent for 4 years, what amount is repaid?
Why does the formula divide by 100?
The simple interest on a sum at 5 percent for 3 years is 900. Find the principal.

solution_steps.explain: Multiply principal, yearly rate and years, then scale by 100.
The payable amount is principal plus interest.

worked_examples.q: Find the simple interest on Rs 8000 at 5 percent per year for 3 years, in rupees.

concepts.title: Celsius to Fahrenheit Conversion
concepts.definition: A Celsius temperature converts to Fahrenheit by scaling it by nine-fifths and shifting by 32 degrees; water boils at 100 C, which maps to 212 F, and freezes at 0 C, mapping to 32 F.
concepts.key_idea: Multiply by 9/5 first, then add 32; reversing the order gives a wrong scale.
question_patterns: Convert 100 degrees Celsius to Fahrenheit using the formula T(F) = T(C) x 9/5 + 32.
What is 0 degrees Celsius on the Fahrenheit scale?

A thermometer reads 37 degrees Celsius. Express this in Fahrenheit.
Why is the offset 32 added only after multiplying by 9/5?

solution_steps.explain: Multiply by 9 to stretch the degree size.
Divide by 5 and add the 32-degree offset.

concepts.title: Volume of a Sphere
concepts.definition: A sphere of radius r fills four-thirds of pi times the cube of its radius, so the volume program cubes the radius with the ** operator and multiplies by 4/3 and pi.
concepts.key_idea: Exponentiation has the highest precedence, so radius ** 3 is evaluated before any multiplication.
question_patterns: Compute the volume of a sphere of radius 7 cm using 4/3 pi r cubed.
Write a Python expression that evaluates the volume of a sphere from its radius.
Find the volume of spheres with radii 12 cm and 16 cm.
Why does radius ** 3 need no brackets in the volume expression?
A sphere's volume is 288 pi cubic cm. Find its radius.

solution_steps.explain: The ** operator raises the radius to the power 3.
Multiply the cube by 4, by pi, and divide by 3.

worked_examples.q: What value does radius ** 3 compute when the radius is 2?

concepts.title: The String Trap of the input Function
concepts.definition: The input() function always hands back a string, so doubling a captured '2' with * repeats the text instead of doubling the number; explicit conversion with int() before multiplying gives the numeric answer.
concepts.key_idea: Everything typed at the keyboard arrives as text, so cast it with int() or float() before arithmetic.
question_patterns: A user types 2 and the program runs num1 = num1 * 2 on the raw input. What is printed and why?

solution_steps.action: show what the string version prints
solution_steps.explain: Repeating one digit twice forms a two-digit number with both digits equal.
After int() conversion, multiplication doubles the value.

concepts.title: Identifier Naming Rules and Keywords
concepts.definition: An identifier names a variable or function: it must start with a letter or underscore, may continue with letters, digits or underscores, cannot contain special symbols or spaces, and must never clash with a reserved keyword such as True or class.
concepts.formula: valid(name) = starts with letter or _ and no keyword
concepts.key_idea: Python is case-sensitive, so Total, total and TOTAL name three different variables.
question_patterns: Why are the names 1st_Room, Total Marks and Hundred$ invalid identifiers?

solution_steps.action: check each name against the rules
solution_steps.explain: Reject names starting with a digit, containing spaces or special symbols, or matching a keyword from the reserved list.
